name: Museum of Contemporary Art Belgrade
funding: Funded by Serbia's Ministry of Culture; the museum publishes the ministry's financial plans for 2023 to 2026.
watch: On 30 January 2020 the government replaced acting director Slobodan Nakarada with Viktor Kiš despite a 2019 open call. Board chair resigned; CIMAM objected.
why_flagged: Funded by Serbia's Ministry of Culture; the museum publishes the ministry's financial plans for 2023 to 2026. No corporate sponsor list found.
records_note: A 2022 report, final accounts for 2020 and 2021, a recent balance sheet and financial plans are posted; no funder list or board is named.

name: Slovak National Gallery
funding: State gallery funded by Slovakia's Ministry of Culture. Its 2025 budget of €13.2M was later cut to €9.6M; admission revenue was about €330,700.
watch: Šimkovičová dismissed director Alexandra Kusá in August 2024 and accused her of a conflict of interest, which Kusá denies. Rallies and a 360-signature letter followed.
why_flagged: State gallery funded by Slovakia's Ministry of Culture. Its 2025 budget of €13.2M was later cut to €9.6M; admission revenue was about €330,700. No corporate sponsor list found.
records_note: Reports of activity and economy run from 2001 to 2025 and accounts are in the Slovak register; no sponsor list or gallery council is posted.

name: Kunsthalle Bratislava
funding: State contributory organisation founded by the Ministry of Culture in 2014 and funded by it. The Kunsthalle said the ministry revoked funding for its 2024 programme on 16 January 2024.
watch: Director Jen Kratochvíl resigned on 15 January 2024. The ministry moved the Kunsthalle under the Slovak National Gallery, citing its programme and efficiency.
why_flagged: State contributory organisation founded by the Ministry of Culture in 2014 and funded by it. The Kunsthalle said the ministry revoked funding for its 2024 programme on 16 January 2024.
records_note: Its own site posts nothing; the parent Slovak National Gallery posts reports for 2001 to 2025 and files accounts in the Slovak register.

name: Museum of Fine Arts Budapest / Hungarian National Gallery
funding: Hungarian state museum. 2026 main and featured sponsors: MVM Group (energy, sells gas), E.ON Energiamegoldások, OTP Bank, MBH Bank, Szerencsejáték Zrt. (state lottery), PPG Trilak, Veolia Energia.
watch: Szerencsejáték also runs Tippmix sports betting; as with Loto-Québec, a state lottery operator is a name to know, not a flag. In April 2026 director László Baán quit the National Cultural Fund committee, writing that many grants did not fit its aims. The minister disputed this.
why_flagged: Hungarian state museum. 2026 main and featured sponsors: MVM Group (energy, sells gas), E.ON Energiamegoldások, OTP Bank, MBH Bank, Szerencsejáték Zrt. (state lottery), PPG Trilak, Veolia Energia.
records_note: It posts yearly budget reports for 2014 to 2025 and budgets to 2026, names its 2026 sponsors, and lists management but no board.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Skopje
funding: Skopje's Town Assembly founded it in 1964 from donated art; Poland gave the building design. The Ministry of Culture and Tourism approves its annual programme projects.
watch: Holds over 5,500 works. Director Mira Gaćina, in post since 2017, resigned for personal reasons after six years; Tihomir Topuzovski is acting director.
records_note: Its site posts the ministry-approved 2025 programme but no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; only staff are named.

name: National Gallery of Arts Tirana
funding: Albanian state museum under the Ministry of Economy, Culture and Innovation, per Wikipedia.
watch: Holds over 5,000 works. Closed for rebuilding with a new annex since 2021, per Wikipedia; in October 2024 the ministry gave no deadline.
records_note: Its official site does not load, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; its ministry publishes no gallery-level accounts that were found.

name: Tirana Art Lab
funding: Independent non-profit founded 2010 by Adela Demetja. Named supporters: Creative Europe, Allianz Kulturstiftung, Pro Helvetia, Robert Bosch Foundation, European Cultural Foundation, Albania's Ministry of Culture, Municipality of Tirana.
watch: No permanent venue from 2018; works with local partners. Runs the Curating with Care programme and the Beyond Matter EU project (2019 to 2023).
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, board or standing funder page; supporters are credited only on individual project pages.

name: National Art Museum of Moldova
funding: State museum subordinate to Moldova's Ministry of Culture.
watch: Holds 39,767 works and had 81,147 visitors in 2024. Its Dadiani wing restoration began in 2004; the second sector opened in September 2021.
records_note: Posts one activity report, for 2024, and yearly management declarations; no audited accounts, funder list or named board members.

name: Latvian National Museum of Art
funding: State-funded museum under Latvia's Ministry of Culture. Its 2025 show Light from Italy was backed by the Italian Embassy, Riga City Council, Rietumu Banka and the ministry.
watch: Sponsor Rietumu Banka was fined €5.85M in 2021 for anti-money-laundering failures. The museum runs six Riga sites, including the Riga Bourse and Arsenāls.
why_flagged: Sponsor Rietumu Banka was fined €5.85M in 2021 for anti-money-laundering failures. The museum runs six Riga sites, including the Riga Bourse and Arsenāls.
records_note: Posts public reports 2019 to 2025 with financial results, budget estimates to 2026 and named 2025 supporters; names a scientific council, not a board.

name: Riga International Biennial of Contemporary Art (RIBOCA)
funding: Private. Founded by Agniya Mirgorodskaya, daughter of Russian fishing businessman Gennady Mirgorodsky. The organisers said funding moved to a US charity, Just A Moment, after 2022.
watch: Curator Žanete Liekīte campaigned against it; four artists withdrew on 30 June 2023. The organisers suspended the third edition in July 2023.
why_flagged: Private. Founded by Agniya Mirgorodskaya, daughter of Russian fishing businessman Gennady Mirgorodsky. The organisers said funding moved to a US charity, Just A Moment, after 2022. No state funder confirmed.
records_note: Its website address is now a parked for-sale page, so its reports, accounts, funders and board are unchecked.

name: National Gallery Prague
funding: State gallery supported by the Ministry of Culture, the Senate and the EU-funded National Recovery Plan. General partner Komerční banka; others include J&T Banka, Bohemia Sekt and Czech Television.
watch: A public call by artists and 23 advisory-board resignations in June 2024 criticised director Knastová. Minister Klempíř dismissed her on 19 March 2026.
why_flagged: State gallery supported by the Ministry of Culture, the Senate and the EU-funded National Recovery Plan. General partner Komerční banka; others include J&T Banka, Bohemia Sekt and Czech Television.
records_note: Annual reports run from 2017 to 2025 and the 2025 report names donors with amounts; no full accounts or board are posted.

name: Ulaanbaatar International Media Art Festival (UBIMAF)
funding: Run by the Arts Council of Mongolia, an NGO. Backers named: Goethe-Institut (2016, 2022), Asia-Europe Foundation, US Embassy and Xacbank (2016), Taiwan Foundation for Democracy (2022). Later editions name none.
watch: The 9th edition ran in May 2024 at the Mongolian National Art Gallery and Red Ger Gallery under the theme Seeing is Believing.
records_note: Its organiser, the Arts Council of Mongolia, posts reports 2003 to 2024 and names its governing council; no accounts or funder list.
